title: CRISP: Fixing Flying Pixels in Latent LiDAR Generation via Diffusion Decoding
claim: Standard decoders blur sharp boundaries and lose voids or gaps; ours preserves them, closely matching ground truth.
layout: 3 columns × 3 rows, top-to-bottom GT/baseline/ours, bracket labels at right
description: A 3×3 grid of LiDAR point-cloud renderings. Each column is a different discontinuity type: scene-scene, object-scene, and object-object, with circled numbers in the headers. Within each column the rows run top to bottom: ground truth in blue, the baseline decoder in green (SVD, Wan, LiDM), and our method CRISP in red. Dotted gray outlines (a rounded box, a tall thin box and a circle) mark the regions of interest. Black leader lines with dots run from these regions to bracketed labels at the right edge of each column. The labels read 'Void lost / Void retained', 'Edge degraded / Edge preserved' and 'Gap lost / Gap retained'. The green rows look noisy and smeared with flying points, while the red rows stay clean and sharp like the blue ground truth. The eye goes first to the contrast between the green and red rows inside the dotted regions.
caption: Qualitative comparison across three frozen latent backbones. Blue denotes the ground-truth point cloud, green the inherited VAE decoder, and red our method (CRISP). The three columns show one failure per backbone: SVD, Wan2.1, and LiDM. Across all cases, CRISP suppresses flying pixels and boundary-bridging artifacts that persist in the baseline reconstructions, yielding cleaner geometry and sharper depth contours.
abstract: Latent LiDAR pipelines suffer from flying pixels: convolutional VAEs blur sharp radial depth discontinuities, yielding edge depths that back-project to points floating between surfaces. We identify this as a major, directly correctable decoder bottleneck and introduce CRISP: a pixel-space diffusion decoder with a backbone-agnostic latent adapter, DiT-based denoiser, and support mask predictor. CRISP replaces video-VAE and LiDAR-native decoders alike while keeping the encoder and latent generator fixed. Across KITTI-360, SemanticKITTI, and nuScenes, replacing only the decoder reduces FSVD/FPVD by 50.5% on average across frozen backbones; for generic video VAEs, the reductions reach 71%/74%. On the LiDAR-native LiDM backbone, FRID drops by 71%, with the largest gains at depth discontinuities. In a pretrained LiDM world model, the same zero-shot replacement improves FSVD by 15.5%, narrowing the sim-to-real gap. Code and checkpoints will be released at https://andrea25512.github.io/CRISP/.
